Congressman Zach Nunn raises concerns over congressional stock trading and touts NDAA amendments
I. S. Corley
U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn, who represents Iowa's Third Congressional District and is based in Des Moines, posted a series of statements on July 22, 2026, addressing congressional stock trading and recent legislative actions.
On July 22, 2026, Nunn alleged significant financial gains among members of Congress from stock market activities: "Republicans and Democrats made $200 million in the stock market last year. There's an investment app that lets you copy the trades of the former Speaker of the House. It's up almost 200% since 2023. The American people can see exactly what's happening here — a blatant double https://t.co/WEVrfaolno". Later that day, he followed up with a brief post referencing an account that tracks public investments by prominent politicians: "Reciepts: @pelositracker https://t.co/0BQUZDc3rI".
In another tweet posted at 20:38 UTC on July 22, Nunn discussed legislative achievements related to national security: "The eight bipartisan amendments we secured in the House-passed NDAA strengthen our national security, support our servicemembers and veterans, and ensure that when we ask Americans to defend this country, they go in with every advantage we can give them. America's security is https://t.co/Pitu2M7JTE".
Nunn's office serves residents across 21 counties in central and southern Iowa (official website). He has prioritized pragmatic and bipartisan policies focused on economic growth, government accountability, agriculture support, family assistance, and national security. Nunn also serves on both the House Financial Services Committee and the House Agriculture Committee. His office provides constituent services related to federal agencies.
